extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent attorneys/agents, and pro se applicants involved in patent prosecution
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for conducting, recording, and scheduling interviews between patent applicants (or their practitioners) and USPTO examiners to advance prosecution of patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and encouragement of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussions between an applicant and an examiner are often indispensable to advance the prosecution of a patent application; interviews that improve mutual understanding of specific issues should be promoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properly conducted interviews can bridge gaps regarding substantive matters, help advance prosecution, and identify patentable subject matter. Positions presented should be advanced with decorum and courtesy.

rubrics_metrics.name: When an interview should be granted
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be granted when the nature of the case is such that the interview serves to develop or clarify outstanding issues in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties should use interview time efficiently, ensure interviews do not extend beyond a reasonable time, minimize interruptions, and consider grouping interviews where effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: All substantive communications are interviews and must be recorded
rubrics_metrics.description: All discussions between the applicant/practitioner and the examiner regarding the merits of a pending application will be considered an interview and are to be made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes any and all records or communications received in connection with the interview via any communication mode. Where an electronic record is created, a copy must be made of record; where not, a summary must be made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.133 interview-location and timing constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews with examiners concerning applications and other matters pending before the Office must be conducted on Office premises and within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate; not permitted elsewhere without Director authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview for the discussion of patentability will not occur before the first Office action unless continuing/substitute or examiner determines it would advance prosecution. Examiner may require scheduling in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews before first Office action — limits and applicant material requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an interview prior to the first Office action is ordinarily granted in continuing or substitute applications; in other applications, an interview before the first Office action is encouraged only if examiner determines it would advance prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may require the applicant requesting such an interview to provide a paper including a general statement of the state of the art, identification of no more than three references believed to be the closest prior art, and an explanation of how the broadest claim distinguishes over such references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Internet communications — authorization required
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet email, instant message system, or video conferencing shall NOT be used to conduct exchanges similar to telephone or personal interviews unless authorization from applicants or an attorney/agent of record has been given to use Internet communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written authorization is preferred (sample provided). Oral authorization is sufficient for arranging video conference interviews only and must be noted in the interview summary or separate communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample written authorization content
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit written authorization recognizing Internet communications are not secure and authorizing USPTO to communicate by video conferencing, instant messaging, or electronic mail, with understanding a copy will be made of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Internet authorization must be submitted on a separate paper entitled to acceptance per 37 CFR 1.4(c) to facilitate processing and avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral authorization limited scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral authorization from the applicant/practitioner is sufficient for video conferencing interviews but is limited to arranging the video conference (including meeting invitation) and does not extend to other communications regarding the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should note details of the oral authorization in the interview summary or a separate communication; written authorization is best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video conferencing must be USPTO-hosted
rubrics_metrics.description: All video conferences for interviews MUST originate or be hosted by USPTO personnel; examiners may not conduct interviews via video conferences hosted by applicants or third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner assigned to the application should coordinate the video conference using USPTO web-based collaboration tools. When applicants request video conferencing, requests should normally be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where/how interviews may be held (in-person, video, telephone)
rubrics_metrics.description: Face-to-face interviews may be via video conferencing or in-person; telephone interviews provide an appropriate level of interaction in some cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-person interviews should be conducted on USPTO premises during normal business hours; if both parties cannot be on the same campus, offer video conference; interviews other than in-person may be held during mutually agreed non-traditional hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote examiner accommodations and campus participation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner is working remotely from a USPTO campus, they should accommodate applicant preference for telephone or electronic communication using USPTO web-based collaboration tools; applicants may request on-campus participation while examiner participates remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate arrangements should be made on campus for equipment/Internet access; USPTO representative may be present with the applicant during on-campus interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and use of AIR / PTOL-413A forms
rubrics_metrics.description: An interview should be arranged in advance to ensure the primary examiner will be available; use the USPTO’s Automated Interview Request (AIR) or the Applicant Initiated Interview Request form (PTOL-413A) to schedule the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms should identify participants, proposed date, communication mode, and include brief description of issues to be discussed. Examiner may be contacted by letter, fax, or email alternatively. A completed Interview Summary form (PTOL-413/413b) should be given or mailed to applicant upon completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and agenda requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney/agent should be fully prepared to discuss issues raised in the Office action at the time of the interview; desirable to submit an agenda in advance, preferably a proposed amendment or argument in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If attorney/agent is not prepared, interview should be rescheduled. Submitting materials in advance permits examiner to prepare and focus on matters set forth in proposed amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize interruptions and be familiar with the file
rubrics_metrics.description: Both parties should avoid unnecessary interruptions during the interview (do not take incoming telephone calls, emails, or text messages unless emergency) and should familiarize themselves with the status and existing issues before the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures efficient use of limited interview time and effective discussion of substantive issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner discretion to end interview or require further action
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should not hesitate to state that claims presented would require further search and consideration, nor to conclude an interview when no common ground can be reached or when application requires further amendment or additional action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should attempt to identify issues and resolve differences as much as possible during interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits — usual interview duration
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the responsibility of all participants to see that the interview is not extended beyond a reasonable period, usually 30 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner must ensure interview does not extend beyond reasonable period; manage agenda and interruptions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews with pro se applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: During an interview with a pro se applicant, the examiner may make suggestions that will advance prosecution, at the examiner’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive time should not be allowed for pro se interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: When agreement is reached — prompt amendment submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Where agreement is reached as a result of an interview, applicant (or applicant’s attorney/agent) should be advised that an amendment pursuant to the agreement should be promptly submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A duplicate copy of a filed amendment/remarks may be sent to the examiner to facilitate early consideration; duplicate copies unnecessary when filed via Patent Center as examiner can access documents quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making substance of interview of record (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete written statement as to the substance of any communication that discussed the merits of an application must be made of record in the application, whether or not an agreement was reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement may be satisfied by submitting a transcript, electronic communication exchange, or Interview Summary form; see 37 CFR 1.133(b) and MPEP §§ 502.03 and 713.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview Summary form required contents (A–I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interview Summary form provides for recordation of: (A) application number; (B) name of applicant; (C) name of examiner; (D) date of interview; (E) type of interview; (F) name of participants; (G) detail all issues discussed; (H) identification of any attachment; and (I) signature of the examiner who conducted the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applicant-initiated interviews, form includes reminder that applicant is responsible to record substance of the interview in the reply to an outstanding action or within the set period if no reply is outstanding. Examiner should provide applicant a copy at end of interview or by mail/email promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Items required in a complete and proper interview summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete recordation should include at least: (A) brief description of nature of any exhibit or demonstration; (B) identification of claims discussed; (C) identification of specific prior art discussed; (D) identification of principal proposed amendments; (E) general thrust of principal arguments of applicant and examiner; (F) general indication of any other pertinent matters; (G) general results or outcome of the interview; (H) for email interviews, a copy of the contents exchanged must be placed in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of arguments need not be lengthy; sufficient if general nature or thrust can be understood in context of file. Applicant may fully describe arguments they deem persuasive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to check accuracy of applicant’s summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to carefully review the applicant’s record of the substance of an interview and correct material inaccuracies which bear directly on the question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If record is not complete or accurate, examiner may give applicant a two-month period to complete reply under 37 CFR 1.135(c) where record of interview is in reply to a non-final Office action. If inaccuracies exist and bear on patentability, examiner should set forth an accurate version in the next official communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to record interview substance may render amendment non-responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply that fails to include a complete or accurate record of the substance of an interview may be non-responsive and applicant may be given a shortened statutory period (two months) to supply omission or correction to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a) but cannot carry date beyond maximum six months set by statute (35 U.S.C. 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited or limited in special situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in unusual situations, interviews are not permitted after submission of an appeal brief or after a notice of allowability has been mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews may be appropriate before applicant’s first reply when examiner suggests allowable subject matter is present or to assist applicant in judging whether to continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and who may be granted interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are generally not granted to persons who lack proper authorization from the applicant or attorney/agent of record; a mere power to inspect is not sufficient authority to grant an interview involving merits of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners not of record can show authorization by completing and signing PTOL-413A. Authorization is not established merely by filing a paper. Certain restrictions apply for suspended/excluded/unregistered attorneys; practitioners must comply with 37 CFR rules (e.g., 1.34, 11.106, 11.505, 11.18).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouped interviews practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouped interviews are effective for attorneys remote from Washington, D.C., who prefer in-person or video conference interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agreement is reached as a result of an interview, applicant should be advised to promptly submit an amendment pursuant to the agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No inter partes questions discussed ex parte
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may not discuss inter partes questions ex parte with any of the interested parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain separation of ex parte proceedings from inter partes issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior exposure of other cases — confidentiality in interview setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to an interview, the examiner should ensure that all files, drawings and other papers, except those necessary in the interview, are out of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect confidentiality of other cases and documents not relevant to the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrations, exhibits, and models handling
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention may be exhibited or demonstrated during the interview by a model or exhibit; a model/exhibit will not generally be admitted as part of the record unless it complies with 37 CFR 1.91.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full description of what was demonstrated/exhibited must be made of record. If video is shown, applicant must demonstrate content bears on outstanding issue and that viewing will advance prosecution; if video format is incompatible with USPTO equipment, applicant should bring necessary equipment. Demonstrations too large to bring into Office may be viewed by examiner outside Office with supervisory approval if essential to clarifying issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration tools and equipment usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaboration tools include USPTO web-based tools; examiners must only use USPTO-supplied equipment and software for interviews and all video conferences for interviews MUST originate or be hosted by USPTO personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures security and recordation consistency for electronic interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after final rejection and prior to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, one interview after final rejection is permitted to place application in condition for allowance or to resolve issues prior to appeal, provided intended purpose/content is presented briefly (preferably in writing) and the examiner is convinced disposal or clarification may be accomplished with only nominal further consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews merely to restate arguments of record or to discuss new limitations requiring more than nominal reconsideration or new search should be denied. A second or further interview may be held if examiner is convinced it will expedite issues for appeal or disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination continued by another examiner — honoring interview agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner who conducted the interview is replaced, the second examiner should ascertain if any agreements were reached and, where conditions permit, take a position consistent with previously reached agreements unless there is a clear error or other prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps preserve expectations and agreements made during interview; see MPEP § 812.01 for related telephone practice.
